questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.questionText:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:
Good public transport networks are the pillars of urban sustainability. Buses, trams, and metro lines can transport big groups of passengers without relying so much on private cars-and therefore eliminating traffic snarls and emissions. Integrated fares across modes of travel make it easy to move around: one ticket could pay for bus, train, and bike-share travel. Spending money on exclusive lanes and priority signaling also makes them faster and more dependable. Nonetheless, constructing and retaining such infrastructure requires capital and long-term vision. Equity issues are also important: lines need to serve low-income communities along with commercial hubs so that all citizens have a benefit. Finally, when properly planned, public transportation promotes economic efficiency, social mobility, and a cleaner city.

Question: What is the central idea of the passage?

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.questionText:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:
Wildlife conservation has increased in importance since governments and NGOs have realized that locals are vital guardians of the environment. Instead of mandating top-down orders, successful initiatives recruit villagers to protect threatened species, serve as informants, and generate income from ecotourism. In other parts of Africa and Asia, community rangers are taught tracking and first aid, while women's organizations produce handicrafts out of sustainable forest products. These programs not only restrict poaching but also create ownership and pride in the maintenance of biodiversity. There are still obstacles, however: low funding levels, human-wildlife conflict, and uncertain land-use rights can undo success.
